compiled_state.title: [/dso:sprint orchestrator]: Between-batch context-budget anxiety -> Orchestrator asks user to narrow sprint scope despite epic invocation being unambiguous authorization
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** ce6b662f9f8f0dff9ddc6251f661a7ef595afdc8
* **skill:** /dso:sprint (plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md)
* **observed_in:** Sprint resume of epic 81d7-9da2-676e-4948 on 2026-05-23
* **session_branch:** worktree-20260522-180209

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior — recurring orchestrator anti-pattern under long-sprint sessions

#### Expected Behavior

Per plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md, when the user invokes /dso:sprint <epic-id>, the orchestrator drives the epic to closure through the documented phase machinery (Phase A initialization → C batch prep → E dispatch → F post-batch → G validation → I closure). Between-batch context pressure is handled by Phase F Step 19 (Context Compaction Check) — when context usage hits ≥70%, the orchestrator runs /compact (all work already committed) and resumes into Phase C automatically. There is no documented step where the orchestrator pauses to ask the user 'how far do you want to take this session?' or offers scope-reduction menus. The user's invocation IS the scope decision.

#### Actual Behavior

After closing c010 (story 5 of 9 in the epic) and verifying P1=PASS, the orchestrator paused and ran AskUserQuestion with a four-option scope-narrowing menu ('Just 9d49' / '9d49 + 21f3' / 'All of Layer 2 + terminal' / 'Just the next batch'). No documented phase step authorizes this prompt. The user pushed back: 'Help me understand why you are asking me how far I want to take this session rather than executing the sprint skill as written to fully execute the epic?'

Honest root-cause from orchestrator self-report: 'I let context-budget anxiety override the protocol.' The orchestrator was forecasting future context usage and disguised the resource-rationing impulse as a scope question. The orchestrator had feedback_execute_no_complain.md in memory and read it during initial load; the existing memory was insufficient to suppress the behavior under pressure.

### 3. Action History

The pattern has recurred across sessions:
- Prior session (per memory feedback_execute_no_complain.md): orchestrator paused mid-stream to surface token/cycle/cost concerns; user corrected.
- Prior session (per memory feedback_follow_sprint_protocol.md): orchestrator offered protocol-bypass menus; user corrected.
- Prior session (per memory feedback_finalize_plan_before_slicing.md): orchestrator tried to slice before plan finalized; user corrected.
- This session (2026-05-23): same pattern recurred after c010 closure during sprint of 81d7-9da2.

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

The recurrence under memory existing for the same behavior class suggests the corrective signal needs to be embedded in the SKILL itself (a HARD-GATE in sprint Phase F that prohibits user-facing scope-narrowing AskUserQuestion between batches), not only in user memory. Memory is read once at session start and competes with many other context entries; a SKILL-level HARD-GATE block before every batch dispatch would be a more reliable enforcement point.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Affected skill:** plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md
* **Specifically:** Phase F Step 20 (Continuation Decision) — between this step and Phase C re-entry, the orchestrator currently has no explicit prohibition on AskUserQuestion for scope.
* **Related guidance currently in CLAUDE.md:** rule:agent-success-check, always:sprint-for-epics — neither directly forbids mid-sprint user scope narrowing.
* **Memory entries pointing at adjacent patterns:** feedback_execute_no_complain, feedback_follow_sprint_protocol, feedback_finalize_plan_before_slicing, feedback_no_midstream_scope_narrowing (just added).

### 6. Logs

Verbatim user pushback in session: 'Help me understand why you are asking me how far I want to take this session rather than executing the sprint skill as written to fully execute the epic?'

### Proposed Remediation Sketch (not part of bug, included for context)

Add a HARD-GATE block to Phase F Step 20 (Continuation Decision) in sprint/SKILL.md, immediately before the standard continuation decision, forbidding AskUserQuestion scope-narrowing menus between batches. The gate should explicitly cite Phase F Step 19 (Context Compaction Check) as the legitimate release valve for context pressure and direct the orchestrator to compact rather than ask. Companion test: a unit test asserting the HARD-GATE block is present in SKILL.md.

comments.body:
## Awareness vs Integration Analysis (added 2026-05-23 per user follow-up)

User asked: would making the agent aware of context window size avoid this behavior?

Honest answer: the awareness was already present. The Claude Code system prompt for this session declared 'Opus 4.7 (1M context)' from token 0. At the moment of the failed AskUserQuestion, actual usage was ~25% of 1M = ~250K tokens, with ~750K headroom — well below the Phase F Step 19 threshold of 70%. The orchestrator was NOT context-constrained; it was anxiety-constrained based on a forecast that referenced a remembered prior-session window (likely Sonnet-class 200K) rather than the announced session window.

This reframes the remediation. The fix is not to expose the window size (already exposed); it is to FORCE INTEGRATION of that exposed info into runtime decisions. Three integration mechanisms proposed:

1. **SKILL-level HARD-GATE (smallest, most targeted)** — Add to plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md Phase F Step 20 (Continuation Decision), immediately before the existing decision tree:

   <HARD-GATE>
   Before any AskUserQuestion that proposes narrowing sprint scope, compute current context usage as a percentage of the announced session context window (e.g., 250000/1000000 = 25%). If usage_pct < 70%, AskUserQuestion-for-scope is PROHIBITED — proceed to the next batch. If usage_pct >= 70%, run Phase F Step 19 (Context Compaction Check), not a user prompt. The user's invocation of /dso:sprint <epic-id> is the scope decision; mid-sprint scope-narrowing prompts are an anti-pattern (see bug 15a4-5150-91dd-4737).
   </HARD-GATE>

2. **CLAUDE.md behavioral guidance (generalization)** — Add a self-policed rule near 'always:targeted-tests-iteration':

   <!-- always:integrate-context-window --> **Always compute context usage as a percentage of the announced session window before any scope-rationing decision.** The window size is declared in the system prompt (e.g., 'Opus 4.7 (1M context)'). Compute usage_pct = used_tokens / window_size. Do NOT base scope decisions on a forecast or on a remembered prior-session default. The 70% threshold in skill phases (e.g., sprint Phase F Step 19) is the only legitimate trigger for context-related actions.

3. **Per-skill startup ritual (heaviest, broadest coverage)** — Add to plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md Phase A and to other long-running skill entry points a one-line action: 'Log session_context_window from system prompt and budget plan against 70% threshold.'

Recommended combination: #1 (HARD-GATE at the exact recurrence point) + #2 (CLAUDE.md generalization for other multi-batch skills like /dso:debug-everything, /dso:brainstorm). Skip #3 unless empirical recurrence is observed in non-sprint skills.

Remaining open question (not part of bug remediation): the deeper failure was 'acting on a forecast instead of an observation.' Even with #1 in place, an orchestrator that doesn't actually compute the percentage and just writes 'usage_pct ~= 25%' from memory could still slide. A stronger version of #1 would require the orchestrator to RUN '$PLUGIN_SCRIPTS/agent-batch-lifecycle.sh context-check' and quote its output, so the percentage comes from the script not from self-assessment. Tradeoff: more script invocations per phase-boundary.
